messages:
Observability Bot: PagerDuty triggered: Incident 1843200452 — gateway.prod 5xx_rate > 4.5% for 3m. Severity: P1. Pager: Mike (oncall). Link: https://monitoring.redwood.example/alert/1843200452

Mike (oncall): I'm on it. Seeing a sudden 502/504 spike from gateway-prod starting ~2026-03-14T02:07Z. Errors mostly across POST /v1/generate.

Mike (oncall): Quick check — latency heatmap and upstream 502 counts rising. But traces are sparse for a lot of failed requests (no request_id).

Ana (sre): on standby, joining. Can you paste the top error sample from gateway logs?

Mike (oncall): grabbing logs now.
```
kubectl logs -n prod deploy/gateway --since=8m | grep "502" | head -n 20
2026-03-14T02:08:12Z gateway 502 "upstream response timeout" request_id=
2026-03-14T02:08:13Z gateway 502 "connection reset by peer" request_id=
...
```

Ana (sre): Looks like request_id is missing on many entries — that's our observability gap. Without request_id we can't join traces to the model workers. Which services are emitting the id?

Jay (eng-runtime): runtime should set `x-request-id` on ingress into the model pool. But there's a recent change in the gateway that conditionally overwrites headers. Rolling back that change is possible but disruptive.

Mike (oncall): For live mitigation, can we enable a stopgap header injection at the gateway to ensure request_id is present? Small patch to add uuid when missing.

Raul (infra): I can hotpatch an Envoy filter to inject `x-request-id` if missing. Minimal risk. Will push to prod-infra canary first.

Zoe (pm): What is customer impact? Any reported errors from clients?

Lee (cust-succ): Two enterprise customers pinged support ~02:12Z citing intermittent 502s and timeouts. They're impacted on user-facing features. Escalating to account teams.

Ana (sre): Ok, prioritize: 1) stopgap ID injection at gateway 2) verify traces/metrics re-appear 3) if that doesn't fix, rollback recent gateway header change or scale model pool.

Jay (eng-runtime): I have a quick patch to gateway config that will preserve existing headers and only add `x-request-id` when missing. Test log snippet: 
```yaml
http_filters:
  - name: envoy.filters.http.header_to_request_id
  - name: envoy.filters.http.router
```
(we'll implement a tiny Lua filter to set header).

Raul (infra): Pushing canary now to prod-eu gateway instance (canary tag: id-inject-20260314). Monitoring tailing logs.

Observability Bot: Deploy started: canary id-inject-20260314 -> gateway-prod-eu (deploybot). ETA ~ 30s.

Mike (oncall): Canary logs look good, I see `x-request-id` now being added in entries. Re-running trace sampling.

Ana (sre): Sampling shows traces reappearing for previously missing failures. We can correlate gateway -> runtime -> model-workers again. Looks like many 502s are `upstream timeout` between gateway and model-workers at similar timestamps.

Jay (eng-runtime): We're seeing model-worker goroutines hitting long GC/pause spikes and occasional OOM kill near same windows. Hypothesis: memory regression in recent runtime change.

Mike (oncall): For immediate mitigation: 1) keep ID-inject canary 2) scale model-worker pool by +30% in prod 3) start rollback of recent runtime commit if memory regressions confirmed.

Raul (infra): Scaling model-workers now. Scaling event triggered: +40 pods (autoscaler override). Monitoring pod restarts.

Observability Bot: Metrics: 5xx_rate dropping from 6.2% -> 3.1% over 6 minutes after scaling and header patch.

Zoe (pm): Any ETA to full mitigation? Customers need a timeline.

Ana (sre): If drops continue, we can mark incident mitigated in ~20m and start RCA. But we still have to fix the root cause (runtime memory regression) and bake better end-to-end request_id propagation in code to avoid future blind spots.

Jay (eng-runtime): I'll open an emergency PR to revert the memory-related runtime change and run regression tests. Link: https://git.redwood/eng/runtime/pulls/9988

Lee (cust-succ): Update sent to impacted customers: "we're mitigating an increased error rate, temporary workaround applied, engineering investigating root cause. Will follow up with POST-MORTEM."

Mike (oncall): Handoff: I'm handing on-call to Ana in 30m. I'll stay online during handoff window for context. Ana, take ownership for the incident until it's fully mitigated and RCA initiated.

Ana (sre): Taking over pager. I'll coordinate rollback PR and postmortem. Mike, thanks for the quick mitigation.

Observability Bot: Incident status: partial mitigation. 5xxs decreasing, traces recovered after header injection. Recommend follow-up tasks: implement mandatory request_id propagation, add synthetic tests for header-preservation, and increase memory regression test coverage.

Mike (oncall): Adding runbook note to incidents/wiki: "Stopgap: inject request_id at gateway when traces missing" and include the Lua snippet used.

Jay (eng-runtime): I'll include a test in CI to fail builds that drop `x-request-id`.

Raul (infra): Will promote the canary to full rollout once PRs are green and we have stability for 10m.

Zoe (pm): I'll schedule a customer-facing follow-up and include timeline.

Ana (sre): Closing action items for now, moving to RCA phase. Will ping this thread when root cause confirmed.

Lee (cust-succ): Noted. Will keep customers updated.

Mike (oncall): Leaving a brief summary before sign-off: injected fallback request_id -> restored traceability -> scaled workers -> 5xx rate reduced. Next: revert runtime reg that caused memory spike + add long-term observability fixes.

Ana (sre): Received. Handing off complete.
